notes: Step 2 identification is uncertain: I read the two gray plates with socket claws as the Light Bluish Gray lego-14704 plates, one on each side of the red 2x2 plate. This is a best guess from a small image.
In step 3 the 11211 brick is assumed to bridge both gray plates, so it gets two edges. The page doesn't show this clearly.
Port assignments on the plates are approximate.
Steps 4 and 5 build the same mirrored arm sub-assembly (hinge plate, clip plate, curved brick), so I recorded it as one repeat with times=2 and a mirror override on copy 2.

Step 4 puts the arm on the model's left and step 5 puts it on the right. I attached both to b4 with null ports, because the images don't show clearly which pieces it joins. The right-hand arm may also touch b2 or b3.
Which hinge studs the clip plate and the curved brick use is approximate.
The black bracket (b5) is already on the model at the start of step 6 with no placement arrow, so I added it here. It is probably attached to b4, and I left the ports null.
Step 7 shows a red piece with studs on the front, and I read it as the inverted bracket 99207 (b7). I'm unsure which pieces it touches, so I joined it to both b5 and b6 with null ports.
The 1 x 2 plate (b6) goes on two studs of the black bracket, as the two arrows in step 6 show.
Step 8 adds the dark red wedge plate 2 x 4 on top of the model. Step 9 looks like the same model with nothing new, possibly a rotated view.
I'm unsure which pieces the wedge plate touches. I joined it to b7 and b6, and left the ports null.
Step 10 looks like the model turned around with no new piece, so I added nothing for it.
Step 11 adds one dark red cheese slope on top. I assumed it goes on a stud of the dark red wedge plate (b8), and left that port null.
Step 12 looks like a view of the model after step 11, so I added nothing for it.
In step 13 I read the small red piece as lego-12825 (tile with clip) and the black piece as the handlebars. They are clipped together first, then placed on top of the model.
I assumed the clip tile (b10) sits on a stud of the dark red wedge plate (b8). That is a guess.
Step 14 shows the finished model with two eye ball joints added on top, one on each side of the handlebars. The page has no callout for them.
I assumed both eyes sit on studs of the dark red wedge plate (b8), and left that port null.
The white tri-tooth plate (b14) is already on the model in step 15 and wasn't shown being placed on earlier pages. I added it here and assumed it is attached to the black bracket b5.
Step 15's callout shows a red 1 x 2 slope. I took it as lego-85984 and joined it to the tooth plate b14. The arrow's exact target is unclear.

Step 16 shows a dark red curved band across the mouth and a dark red wedge plate below, but no callout shows them being placed. I added nothing for step 16. They are probably 93273 and the second 51739, and later pages may show them.
Page 10 starts a new sub-assembly, probably a leg or foot, shown in the preview at top-left. It is built once on this page. A later page may repeat it, and I haven't assumed that.
In step 3 the red piece's studs point up into the underside of the gray towball plate. I read it as lego-3665, the inverted slope. The catalogue lists no studs on it, so I left its ports null.
The sub-assembly is not yet attached to the main model.
Sub-step 4 adds a second dark bluish gray towball plate (b20) with a red 1 x 2 plate (b21) on top, then fixes it to the leg. I joined b20 to b19, but the contact is not clearly shown.

Step 17 shows the main model with the leg attached. A dark red curved band across the mouth and a dark red wedge plate on the front also appear, with no placement callout. I took them as lego-93273 (b22) and the second lego-51739 (b23). Their attachment points are guesses and the ports are null.
The leg is joined to the body through b16 and b23. How the leg attaches to the body is unclear, so that edge is a guess.
Page 12 builds the second leg, a mirror of the page 10 leg. Steps 1 to 3 are the same, so I recorded it as separate parts rather than a repeat, because ids continue from earlier turns.

The parts list has two lego-14417 and two lego-14419 in dark bluish gray. The step 1 plates of both legs are therefore probably 14417, and the step 4 plates are probably 14419. Earlier I typed b20 as 14417, and it is probably 14419.
This leg is not yet attached to the model.

Sub-step 4 mirrors the first leg's sub-step 4 on the second leg. The gray plate is typed lego-14419, following the parts-list count (two 14417 and two 14419). The plate in the same step on the first leg, b20, is probably 14419 too.
Step 18 attaches the second leg to the body. As with the first leg, I joined it to b23 with null ports. The exact contact is a guess.
Step 19 is only a rotate-the-model view, as the arrow icon shows, so it adds nothing.
The back of the model shows the two flame pieces (lego-85959pat0003) already attached, and no step has placed them yet. I will add them if a later page shows the placement.
Page 15 is a rotate-the-model view with no building step.
Page 17 is an advertisement with no building step.
Page 18 is a Mixels collection catalogue with no building step.
Page 19 is a game advertisement with an in-game code and no building step.
Page 20 is a survey promotion and legal text with no building step.

The two flame pieces (lego-85959pat0003), the second lego-61252, the two lego-14704 attachment points and the other unplaced parts never appeared in an explicit step. Their attachment to the finished model is not recorded.

Correction: b20 is re-emitted as lego-14419, replacing its earlier lego-14417 type. It is the dark bluish gray towball-socket plate in the first leg's sub-step 4. This gives two 14417 (b16, b24) and two 14419 (b20, b28), which matches the parts list.

The checker flagged seven piece types as missing. The booklet pages I received never show them being placed, and they must be in the finished model, so I added them to match the inventory. The pieces are lego-3020, two lego-3069b, lego-3710, three lego-3794b, a fourth lego-54200 and two flames lego-85959pat0003.

I guessed where these go. b30 (2x4 plate) joins the wedge b8, and the tiles, 1x4 plate and jumpers build on it. The fourth cheese slope b37 goes on b8. The flames b38 and b39 are on the back sockets b2 and b3. The edges use null ports because the pages show no placement.
The first pages hide some of the 'red stripe' lower body in step 3 of page 2. The tiles, plate and jumpers may belong there instead.
